newsitem.title: USA: Savannah Foods merges with Florida Crystals.
newsitem.headline: Savannah Foods merges with Florida Crystals.

text.p: Sugar refiner and distributor Savannah Foods & Industries Inc said Tuesday it agreed to merge with Florida Crystals Inc, the Florida-based sugar and related operations of privately-held Flo-Sun Inc.
The company said that the merged entity will have current annual revenues on a pro-forma basis of about $1.5 billion and assets in excess of $1 billion.

Flo-Sun will hold 39.4 percent of the equity in the merged company, other Florida Crystals shareholders will hold 19.1 percent of the equity and the remaining 41.5 percent will be held by Savannah Foods' shareholders, the company said.

The Flo-Sun shares will be weighted at eight times ordinary shares for voting purposes and will represent about 83 percent of the voting power of the outstanding shares. All other shares will have one vote per share, Savannah said.
The company said that the deal is expected to lower costs through pre-tax synergies of about $20 million and help stabilize the company's cyclical earnings.

In a statement, R. Eugene Cartledge, chairman of Savannah, said, "Management believes that all of these factors, while they will result in earnings per share lower than the current cyclical peaks, should result in a stronger combined company that can command a higher P/E multiple for the stock."

"We believe this merger is the best method to assure long-term value to Savannah Foods' stockholders in light of the increasingly competitive environment for sugar refiners, the likelihood of significant refining over-capacity and the difficulty in obtaining raw sugar in such an environment," he said.

Alfonso Fanjul, chairman and chief executive officer of Florida Crystals and J. Pepe Fanjul, Florida Crystal's vice chairman, president and chief operating officer, will both assume the same positions in the combined company, Savannah said.
William Sprague, president of Savannah Foods, will be president of the new company's refining division.
The transaction is subject to the approval of the Savannah Foods' shareholders and is expected to close in October.
